tossups.text: One poem by this author describes a "horrible thing / which raced sideways while blowing bubbles" during the title characters' beach trip. Another of this author's poems repeats different permutations of the phrases "spring summer autumn winter" and "sun moon stars rain." This poet of "maggie and milly and molly and may" wrote of someone "more brave than me:more blond than you" in another poem. For 10 points, name this American poet of "anyone lived in a pretty how town" and "i sing of Olaf glad and big," known for his lack of capitalization.

Recent excavations in this country's Bose Basin have unearthed the Acheulian axe, which repudiates the theory of the Movius Line. In 2012, the largest ever feathered dinosaur, of genus Yutyrannus, was discovered in this country. A French anthropologist working in this country argued that galactic, earth, life and consciousness were the four types of evolution, which he incorporated into his later book The Phenomenon of Man. In 1978, the elongated, fossilized skull of Dali Man was found in this country, providing some physical evidence of man in the Pleistocene. Johan Gunnar Andersson found two teeth in a cave near this country's "Chicken Bone Hill." A Jesuit anthropologist working in this country named Pierre Teilhard de Chardin worked with Davidson Black to discover the fossilized remains of a Homo Erectus in the Western Hills near Zhoukoudian. For 10 points, name this country of origin of Peking Man.

Among his works for solo organ are Three Rhapsodies on Breton Melodies, and he wrote two cello concertos, Op. 33 in A minor and Op. 119 in D minor. His symphonic poems include La jeunesse d'Hercule and Le rouet d'Omphale. His most famous opera features the aria "Mon coeur s'ouvre à ta voix" and a famous bacchanal. Another of his works contains a movement which quotes Rossini's "Una voce poco fa," Fossils, as well as ones entitled Aquarium, Pianists, and The Swan. For 10 points, identify this French composer of Samson and Delilah, the Organ Symphony, and The Carnival of the Animals.

Stockmayer fluids of dipolar molecules can be simulated using one of these plus a term for dipole-dipole interactions. Extremely accurate for noble gases, it is inaccurate for open shells or for metallic applications due to delocalized electrons. Including variables for well depth and hard sphere diameter, it equals zero when r equals the hard sphere diameter. It expresses the balance between long distance van der Waals attractions and short distance Pauli repulsion forces. Also called the 6-12 potential, FTP, identify this mathematical model which can be used to represent the interactions between two neutral molecules.

This thinker described an "arc of culture" that different peoples would draw from to create individual cultures in a work that used adjectives like "restraint" and "abandon" to describe different tribes. This thinker described a type of moral debt known as "giri" that is repaid through "clearing one's name." This thinker analyzed the Zuni, Dobu, and Kwakiutl [KWAH-kee-YOO-tul] in a work that defined culture as "personality writ large." This author of Patterns of Culture wrote a book which contrasted Japan's shame culture with the U.S.'s guilt culture. For 10 points, name this American anthropologist who wrote The Chrysanthemum and the Sword.

This person names a family of proteins encoded for by genes in the phage 933W. The growth of genera named for Theodor Escherich and this person on the newly-invented LB medium allowed isolation of the P2 phage. The Vero cell line is susceptible to a family of proteins named for this person that is the cause of the thrombotic microangiopathy STEC-HUS. This person names proteins that are imported by binding to globotriaosylceramide and act by cleaving an adenine in the sarcin-ricin loop. Those proteins named for this person cause hemolytic-uremic syndrome and are released by the O157H7 strain. In 1897 this scientist found that bacteria dysentery is caused by a namesake genus that is nested within Escherichia. For 10 points, name this Japanese bacteriologist who names the toxins produced by enterohemorrhagic E. coli.

Instances of these devices with stacked lamination uses an alternate method of E and I laminations. Large ones can use oil for insulation. Scott-t ones can handle two to three phase connections. Their components can be in delta or wye configurations. The cores of these devices can be three, four, or five limbed. Electric audio amplifiers, particularly those in a class b, use center tapped ones on the input and the output. The ratio of voltages associated with one of these devices is proportional to the ratio of turns. They can be used to step up or down voltage. For 10 points, name these devices that transfer electrical energy from one AC circuit to another using induction.

One short story in this book sees the villainous cobras Nag and Nagaina killed by the title mongoose defending a family of humans. That story is "Rikki-Tikki-Tavi." One character in this book is adopted by Messua after being raised by Raksha the wolf. That character kills the lame tiger Shere Khan in this book. For 10 points, name this collection of stories that includes three stories about the "man-cub" Mowgli, a work by Rudyard Kipling.

A court ruled that this philosopher was "morally unfit" to teach, partially due to his challenges of traditional sexual morality in Marriage and Morals. In another work, this man analyzed sentences referring to non-existent objects such as "the present king of France is bald." This author of On Denoting resolved his namesake paradox with the theory of types, and he argued that the Church is the "principal enemy of moral progress" in the essay Why I Am Not a Christian. For 10 points, name this British philosopher who, along with Alfred North Whitehead, wrote Principia Mathematica.

This author criticized the widespread use of "dying metaphors" in the essay "Politics and the English Language." In a novel by this author, Mr. Frederick uses dynamite to blow up a windmill. The protagonist of another novel by this author works in the Ministry of Truth, and is tortured with rats in Room 101. This author wrote a novel in which Manor Farm is overtaken by Napoleon the pig, and a novel about Winston Smith's struggle against Big Brother. For 10 points, name this author of Animal Farm and 1984.

Nei and Lin used this letter used to represent the nucleotide diversity in a population. This letter names a theorem that describes how an equation with n variables, in k dimensions can be rewritten in terms of n-minus-k parameters. A quantity denoted by this letter is equal to the pressure needed to prevent water movement across a semipermeable membrane. Huckel's rule states that a cyclic system with "4n plus 2" electrons in these orbitals is aromatic. Double bonds in alkenes consist of a sigma bond and a bond denoted by his letter. For 10 points, name this letter which is used to symbolize a constant equal to the ratio of a circle's circumference to diameter.

Ramsey-Boiteux pricing concerns the social welfare-maximizing pricing scheme in this market condition, for which the value of the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index is maximized. Joan Robinson coined the term for a symmetrical version of this situation, whose occurrence requires a lack of substitutes and absence of price discrimination. Price exceeds marginal revenue in this kind of system, which exhibits deadweight loss since the marginal cost to the consumer is lower than the set price. For 10 points, name this economic situation in which one seller entirely controls the market for a good or service.

In a 2012 paper, Michael Bobick analyzed the rise of this region's largest company through illegal cigarette and frozen food trade. Almost everything in this region is run by the company Sheriff, which also produces its iconic Kvint brandy. 1,500 troops making up the OGRT have occupied this region with the pretext of controlling an ammunition depot at Cobasna. This region attempted to shut down schools that taught using a Latin alphabet instead of Cyrillic, in addition to cracking down on the spread of Romanian. This region's Bendery ("ben-derry") Military Museum and the parliament building in Tiraspol are among its many relics preserved from when it was a part of the Soviet Union. For 10 points, name this breakaway region which gets its name from the river that demarcates the Ukraine-Moldova border.

One country in this conflict was ruled by its chancellor William Longchamp while its king participated; it was preceded by a crushing defeat at the Horns of Hattin, after which Guy de Lusignan and Raynald Chatillion were taken prisoner. Ending shortly after the Battle of Arsuf, at which one key player was Robert de Sablé, this campaign, called for by Gregory VIII and led in part by Phillip II Augustus of France, also included a Siege of Acre in 1190. For 10 points, name this conflict in which Richard Lionheart befriended his foe Saladin while failing to re-conquer Jerusalem.

The long opening stage direction in this play mentions a light source "which fights its way through" a "little window." In this play's first act, one character exclaims "DAMN MY EGGS!" and a young boy is given fifty cents for a school activity. In this play's second act, Bobo reveals that he was unable to meet Willy Harris in Springfield. Joseph Asagai is a character in this play who plans to marry Beneatha and move to Africa. This play details the struggles of the Younger family as they debate what to do with a $10,000 life insurance check. For 10 points, name this play that takes its title from a Langston Hughes poem and was written by Lorraine Hansberry.

In Irish myth, Athairne ("AH-hair-nuh") used magic to explode containers holding this commodity while he was still a fetus. A fairy named Little Wildbeam was dedicated to protecting this commodity. After fir cones and bear saliva prove useless, nectar from a distant island finally enables Osmotar ("OHSS-moh-tar") to create this commodity. A woman who sells this commodity comforts Gilgamesh and may have been the goddess Siduri. In ancient Sumer, the goddess Ninkasi was the mistress of this substance. The Norse gods pay a visit to Hymir ("HOO-mare") to fulfill a quest from Aegir ("AH-year") to procure a cauldron big enough to make lots of this substance. Some of this substance colored to look like blood was used to pacify the rage of Sekhmet ("SEK-met"). For 10 points, name this alcoholic beverage which the Greeks considered less manly than wine.

In one of this man's works, an urn-bearing woman and two torch-carrying girls proceed into a door under the inscription "Uxori optimae Albertus". In addition to that pyramidal tomb for Duchess Maria Christina, he sculpted a statue that stands next to a Robert Adam staircase in Apsley House and depicts an orb topped by a gilded Nike in the right hand of a man posing as Mars the Peacemaker. A woman's head lolls back as she reaches her arms up towards her winged lover in one of this man's sculptures, while the subject of another holds an apple in her hand as she poses, nude from the waist up, on a couch. For 10 points, name this Venetian neoclassical sculptor of Psyche Revived by Cupid's Kiss and Paulina Borghese as Venus Victrix.

Edwin Salpeter confirmed the discovery of the first of these objects to be identified. Daily variation by at least one order of magnitude is demonstrated in the optically violent variable type of these objects. One of these appears as four distinct objects, called the Einstein Cross. The oldest known one of these objects was formed during the universe's structure formation stage. The first of these objects to be discovered was located in the constellation Virgo and was notable for its high redshift. These objects are powered by the gravitational accretion in supermassive black holes. For 10 points, name these very bright and very distant radio sources.

Several months after this event, the President explained his denial about it by saying that "my heart and my best intentions still tell me that's true, but the facts and the evidence tell me it is not." Robert McFarlane came up with the scheme that led to this scandal, which resulted from a violation of the Boland Amendment. The Tower Commission implicated John Poindexter and Oliver North in this scandal. For 10 points, name this Reagan-era scandal, in which money from weapon sales in a Middle Eastern country where diverted to fight the Sandinistas in Nicaragua.

The "Ballroom of Death" and the "Popcorn Field" are treacherous areas on the path through this mountain's Khumbu Icefall. The South Col is a pass from Lhotse to this mountain within the "death zone" over 8,000 meters. An April 2014 avalanche on this mountain killed sixteen Sherpa guides. For 10 points, name this peak in the Himalayas first summited by Tenzing Norgay and Sir Edmund Hillary, the tallest mountain in the world.

parts.text: Name this author. In another novel by this author, Mariam kills her abusive husband Rasheed to save her friend Laila's life.

This novel by Hosseini is titled for the role Hassan played for Amir in competitions they played in as children. In the second half of this novel, Amir journeys to Afghanistan to rescue Hassan's son Sohrab.

Sohrab is held by Assef, a member of this Islamic militant group. Mariam's confession to this group allows Laila to escape Kabul, although she is later able to return after the United States goes to war with this group.

bonuses.leadin: In a novel by this author, General Taheri's daughter confides in her future husband that her mother suffered a stroke after she ran away from home with another man. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this idea which states that within science, the rewards accrue disproportionately to those who already possess notoriety.
The "Matthew effect" was coined by this social scientist better known for his work on the role of anomie in deviance, a part of his strain theory. He also wrote On the Shoulders of Giants.
This work is Merton's most important work, which is notable for charting a middle course between data collection and totalizing theories by advocating "theories of the middle range."
acceptableAnswers: The Social Theory and Social Structure

parts.text: Known for their supernatural themes and fantastical images, this movement's adherents include Alberto Giacometti, Giorgio de Chirico and Joan Miro.
This surrealist worked with Luis Bunuel on films such as An Andalusian Dog, but is better known for paintings featuring his "Soft Watches" like The Persistence of Memory.

This Mexican surrealist is known for self-portraits like the one in which two images of herself sit next to each other on a bench holding hands, their hearts connected by an artery in midair. She was married to Diego Rivera.

parts.text: Name this disabled British scientist who names a form of black body radiation predicted to be released from black holes as they have finite non-zero temperature and entropy, allowing them to fade away over time.
Hawking Radiation is sometimes also named after this Mexican Scientist who also helped to develop the no-hair theorem

The no-hair theorem states that the black hole solutions of the Einstein Maxwell equations can be classified using only three externally observable classical parameters, mass, angular momentum and this other quantity.

parts.text: Identify this legally mandated value, whose impact Card and Krueger analyzed by phoning hundreds of New Jersey and Pennsylvania restaurants.
A writer who has cited that study is this Nobel laureate with a New York Times column.

Republicans generally favor this program, which allows some poor workers to get a refund larger than their withholdings. Krugman argues that the amount of this benefit should be increased along with the minimum wage.

parts.text: The seven crystal systems contain the point lattices. Give the alternate name for these fourteen point lattices, named for the scientist that proved that only fourteen were possible.
Name the crystal system with the second lowest symmetry, with two ninety-degree angles and three unequal sides.
White tin is the only element with this crystal structure at room temperature. Name the crystal structure also found in austenite.

bonuses.leadin: 19. Identify the following about crystal structures FTPE.

parts.text: K-selecting organisms tend to have population sizes near this quantity, the maximum amount of individuals that can be sustained in a given environment.

Factors that are "dependent" on this quantity are thus generally more significant to K-selecting organisms than r-selecting ones. Logistic population growth occurs in a manner "dependent" on this quantity.
acceptableAnswers: I guess prompt on population size

parts.text: r-selecting organisms tend to follow this type of survivorship curve. These concave-up curves involve many individuals dying early in their lifespan, with a few survivors living for a long time.

bonuses.leadin: Organisms may employ the evolutionary strategies of either r or K selection. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this novel, in which Dr. Pangloss repeatedly survives death while maintaining that "all is for the best in this best of all possible worlds."
This French satirist wrote Candide. His plays include Zaire and Mahomet.
Candide travels to this South American utopian society, which he leaves with a herd of red pack sheep piled with gold and jewels.

bonuses.leadin: This novel's protagonist searches for Cunegonde while travelling the world with Martin and Cacambo. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this thinker whose most famous work declares "Woman is born free and lives equal to man in her rights." That document was titled in reference to a document drafted by Lafayette and Jefferson to present to the National Assembly.

This author's masterpiece was written in response to de Gouges and a speech by Talleyrand-Perigord. This author argued that women should be educated in the same way as men in A Vindication of the Rights of Woman.
Wollstonecraft's Vindication of the Rights of Men was written during a pamphlet war as a response to this Whig's Reflections on the Revolution in France.

parts.text: A governess tries to protect Miles and Flora from the ghosts of Miss Jessel and Peter Quint in this novella by Henry James.
In this Charles Dickens novella, Ebenezer Scrooge is visited by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Christmas Present, and Christmas Yet to Come.
This author wrote about Eleanor Vance's possession by ghosts in The Haunting of Hill House, but is better known for writing about Tessie Hutchinson in "The Lottery."

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about ghosts in literature, for 10 points each.

parts.text: In glycolysis, a pathway that is part of cellular respiration, this enzyme reversibly cleaves fructose-1,6-bisphosphate to form DHAP and G3P, which the enzyme triosephosphate isomerase converts between.

Physiological respiration in humans is controlled by a system of chemoreceptors in the medulla oblongata, pons, and brainstem that trigger breathing in response to the effect of this gas on the pH of the blood.
Contraction of the diaphragm muscle increases the volume of chest cavity and creates this kind of pressure compared to atmospheric pressure, forcing air into the lungs.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about various types of respiration, for 10 points each.

Although she was unable to perform field research in this nation during World War 2, Benedictproposed the existence of a "shame culture" in this Asian country in The Chrysanthemum and the Sword.
This other student of Boas, a French anthropologist, held his teacher as he died. One of his mostinfluential studies was The Savage Mind.

parts.text: Name this cryptid, now an icon of Point Pleasant and West Virginia at large, generally depicted as a tall, winged humanoid with glowing red eyes, but little in common with its namesake insect.
Further down the coast, this swamp-dwelling cryptid is often seen as Florida's answer to Bigfoot, and is named for its foul odour.
acceptableAnswers: Esti Capcaki from players with truly impressive Seminole knowledge

parts.text: Name this leader who delivered the "I am Prepared to Die" speech during the Rivonia trial. After being freed from prison, this leader became the first Black head of state of South Africa in 1994.

Nelson Mandela was married to this woman, who carried on his activist work while he was in prison. This woman was accused of kidnapping and torturing South African government collaborators through her security detail, the Mandela United Football Club.
Most of Winnie Mandela's unsavory activities were focused in this township near Johannesburg. Students protesting racist policies were fired on by police in a 1976 "uprising" in this township.

Death of a Salesman is by this playwright of The Crucible.
In this other Miller play, Eddie Carbone informs immigration officials that Marco and Rodolpho are undocumented in order to prevent Rodolpho's marriage to Catherine.

parts.text: Name this wife of Menelaus, whose kidnapping by Paris sparked the Trojan War.

In the play Helen, the title character is actually taken by the gods to this kingdom, where she narrowly escapes marriage to Theoclymenus. In real life, the syncretic god Serapis was worshiped here after its conquest by Alexander.
In a myth often depicted in art, Menelaus threatened to kill Helen during the sack of Troy, but spared her after she killed her husband and performed this other action.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on begging for her life

parts.text: This term refers to pianists slightly speeding up and slowing down the tempo of a piece to make their playing more expressive. It is commonly employed while playing Chopin pieces.
Many pieces call for pianists to play these broken chords, in which the notes of a chord are played one at a time.
Most pianos have three of these features. The leftmost of them softens the notes, while the rightmost one is used to sustain notes after they are played.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name these techniques used by piano players.

parts.text: Name this ground layer consisting of perennially frozen soil. This layer is common in Siberia and Arctic Canada.
These landforms can form when hydraulic pressure pushes a lens of permafrost up, deforming the active layer. These hill-like structures with ice cores are common in the Tuktoyaktuk Peninsula.

The melting of ice wedges that span the active layer and permafrost can result in features described by this term and preceded by the prefix "thermo." This term describes areas where soluble carbonate rocks result in numerous sinkholes and cave systems.

bonuses.leadin: The zero curtain separates this layer from the active layer above it, which periodically thaws. For 10 points each:

This current director of the CIA was previously a 4-star general who commanded US forces in Iraq and Afghanistan.
This former director of the CIA gave up his spot in mid-2011 in order to serve as Secretary of Defense under the Obama administration, replacing the retiring Robert Gates.

parts.text: The Ghost Army made inflatable kinds of these armored land vehicles. The largest battle between these vehicles was in Kursk.

A huge factory owned by this company was disguised by building a fake town on its roof to fool potential aerial reconnaissance. This company also produced the first commercial jet airliner made in the US, the 707.
Operation Fortitude South led Germany to think Calais was this event's target. This event saw troops land on beaches with codenames such as Omaha and Juneau.
